0B5A5B1254EE88FF: Assemble the TFMG tower from its controller, steel fluid tanks and one output for every cut. Supply crude from a surveyed petroleum province and isolate each product buffer.

For the first run, feed Railcraft creosote from the coke works into a TFMG firebox below the tower. Connect its exhaust to an exhaust outlet; a full exhaust buffer stops firing. Creosote primes the refinery before it has distilled its own fuel.

Prime the controller with the earlier steam-mixed lubricant. Once the tower runs, collect fuels and naphtha separately; keep the coke works, rail tank yard and refinery linked by labeled transfer lines.
04EDCB87A68F7B52: Build a Stellaris oxygen tank from the live LV-gated recipe and make all four pieces of the Stellaris space suit before departure.
Feed suitable grain to adult TFC sheep until they are familiar enough to produce wool, then shear them when wool is available. Spin wool with a spindle, weave yarn into cloth, then weave white wool.
Pan ore deposits in claystone or dolomite using fresh water to find raw amethyst. Grind it in a quern fitted with a handstone.
Make the visor through TFC glassworking: heat a suitable batch such as hematitic glass, apply amethyst powder, pour into a brass-plated basin, let it cool and cut it with a gem saw.
Fill tanks in the water separator’s oxygen output slot. Wear the chestplate and crouch-use a charged tank to transfer oxygen; check its gauge and carry a separate reserve.
06D83DFD0A495597: Mine and return with sixteen raw desh from the Moon. Use a TFC bronze, wrought-iron or better pickaxe for the iron-grade lunar blocks.

After the lunar visit, unload at least sixteen raw desh into your inventory on Terra to record the return. Finished desh still requires the blast-furnace route; keep a return reserve.
26FFE1882978622D: Stock sixteen raw desh from ordinary lunar mining. Use a TFC bronze, wrought-iron or better pickaxe.

Vent CO2 continuously from a side outlet through MI pipes into a TFMG Exhaust; the top fluid port is unused. Each coal releases 36 L of CO2 during processing. For first-steel startup, process 35 coal: reserve 32 coke and crush the other three into fresh coke dust.
1CE701199DF997EE: Stage eight bauxite dust, two desh ingots, and two tharsite ingots.

17138C41AFEA7B9E: Produce and buffer 8,000 mB of Stellaris fuel.
The live Create mixing bridges TFMG kerosene, gasoline, or diesel into equal-volume rocket fuel; use fixed tanks and preserve a return share.
Fill vanilla buckets with Stellaris fuel under a Create spout, then use the rocket fuel input. Keep biomass for its industrial consumers.
05E487281942D4A6: Travel to the Stellaris Mars dimension, establish a safe route home, and return with Mars Tharsite for the next industrial stage.

With the basic 3,000 mB tank, depart for Mars full and carry three additional fuel buckets for the return. Crouch-open the lander to recover the rocket with its remaining fuel; bring launch-pad equipment, oxygen and mining tools.
063E964BB6CF6EA6: Produce four MI digital circuits with the current clean-processing route.
Buffer wafers, boards, fine wire, and assembly outputs; AE2 will coordinate this line, not replace it.

PRE-02 unlocks the MI electronic-circuit sapphire prototype; PRE-03 unlocks the Mekanism advanced-control prototype. Pan TFC chalk-region deposits in fresh water for raw sapphire, then polish it with TFC sandpaper; keep boards, TFMG transistors and capacitors supplied.
0F16DEDF6E39443D: Batch sixteen bronze ingots and sixteen ordinary industrial iron dust with your kinetic and bronze-steam workshop.

After Industrial Heat research, mill earned TFC wrought-iron ingots in the MI macerator: one ingot makes one iron dust. Keep TFC first metallurgy and the bronze boiler, water and fuel supplies working.
6D8EE28E14590C42: Stage thirty-two ordinary MI iron dust and thirty-two TFMG coal coke.
Prepare the dust from earned TFC wrought-iron ingots in the MI macerator under Industrial Heat research. The handoff keeps one ingot per dust and the native processing cost.
Use the retained iron-dust industrial-blasting route with flux and its required hot-air supply. Provide empty storage for molten slag and furnace gas before starting.
46F7529D4A6574CB: Stock thirty-two Create tracks and sixteen wrought-iron ingots.
Keep them at the yard where a maintenance cart can reach either end of the line.

For wrought iron, hammer normal hematite into rocky chunks, sluice them into chunks, quern those into dirty dust, then sluice again for clean hematite powder. Feed the upper sluice inlet with the shallow flow seven horizontal steps from a fresh-water source; keep the lower outlet clear.

Four normal ores give twenty clean powders. Craft five pellets, turn four into one briquet, and charge the formed bloomery with that briquet, the spare pellet and one stack of two charcoal. Ignite, close and wait for the bloom. This batch supplies one ingot; repeat sixteen times for this stock.

Build a bronze anvil before forging the bronze sheets for the bloomery. On that anvil, hammer the hot raw bloom into a refined bloom, then into wrought iron. Keep the chamber insulated and the blooms hot enough to work.
04C35F62E0D31D66: Build a hollow 3×3×3 Railcraft coke oven from 26 coke oven bricks, with full top and bottom layers and air in the center. Seven crafts make 28 bricks, leaving two spare. Each TFC oak log produces one charcoal and 250 mB of creosote; leave room for both outputs.

In the MI Bronze Mixer, combine 500 mB of Railcraft creosote and one redstone to make 500 mB of MI lubricant. Supply steam from the bronze boiler throughout mixing; this recipe uses 2 EU/t for 100 ticks.

Convert each 1,000 mB of MI lubricant into 1,000 mB of TFMG lubrication oil in an andesite mechanical mixer, with a basin two blocks below. No burner is needed. One small water wheel at 8 RPM can drive this mixer at 8 RPM: its 4 SU load fits the 8 SU source and andesite limit.

Eight oak logs and four redstone supply two litres of oil through four Bronze Mixer batches and two mechanical mixing batches. Boiler water and fuel, the machines and their construction materials are additional supplies. Keep a dedicated oil buffer tank.

Keep steam, creosote, lubricant and oil pipe networks separate. Keep basin extraction disabled while feeding and mixing; stop lubricant feed and wait for the input to empty before extracting the finished oil. Drain the output before the next batch.

Form vanilla buckets in the MI Steel Packer: three steel curved plates make four buckets. Pipe 1,000 mB of TFMG lubrication oil into a Create spout and place an empty vanilla bucket on a depot two blocks below it. Refill the spout for each bucket.

Oil mixing consumes 800 mB of steam. Precharge a separate bronze boiler with 2,000 mB of ordinary steam, leaving 1,200 mB after these four jobs and before other use. The casing and steel-steam bucket route needs eight new steel ingots beyond the earlier ignition/shaft pair. Fill two of its four buckets with these two litres of oil and retain two empty buckets. Boiler heat-up water and fuel, construction parts and other machine use are additional supplies.
15F09D0C13ED7C79: Craft a Water Flasks leather flask.
Fill it before departure and keep a known fresh-water point on the return route.

For early leather, take a small sheepskin hide from a TFC sheep killed by the player and use a knife to make a small raw hide. Knap a sedimentary stone knife and axe; gather oak twigs for their handles and two oak logs from a cool, wet oak forest. Keep one log as the scraping surface.

Make three oak barrels (seven oak lumber each) and one wooden bucket (three lumber). Reuse the bucket to put 1,000 mB of fresh water in each barrel. In barrel B, two flux make 1,000 mB of limewater; add one raw hide and seal it. In barrel A, seal one oak log with the water to make tannin.

Place the soaked hide on top of the spare oak log with air above it, then scrape all sixteen cells with the knife. Seal the scraped hide in barrel C to rinse it into a prepared hide; seal that hide in barrel A's tannin to get one leather. Each sealed recipe has a 7,200-calendar-tick duration; let it finish before opening. The three hide steps use 300 mB each and leave 700 mB in each barrel. Repeat the leather batch for the flask's displayed recipe.
0C462947C2A27098: This objective checks one cured natural-rubber sheet. Each 500 mB of resin makes one rubber, then one pressed sheet; an optional first stock batch of eight sheets uses 4,000 mB.

Tap a naturally grown GTCEu rubber tree in warm, wet TFC terrain. Leave an air block between the sapper and trunk, with at least two matching trunk blocks and five natural leaves nearby. Make the sapper's leather through the earlier TFC hide-and-tannin work. One solitary sapper produces 100 mB per completed cycle: five cycles for one sheet, forty for the eight-sheet stock batch.

For this route, run two steel batches with 36 separate 8-L furnace-gas tanks and 10 separate 8-L CO₂ tanks. Budget two 55-L hot-air charges, six coke dust, two iron dust and two flux; carry the fuel timer and stored gases between runs. Disable tuyere insertion while charging. Before firing, stop intake/stove feed, switch hot-air banks to extraction and enable the tuyere. Stonecut one ingot into two TFMG rebar. One rebar plus flint makes the ignition tool; consume it with three iron ingots and two string for the flint bow. Keep the other steel ingot for the plate and shafts. Follow the existing Beneath route, manufacture an empty burner and capture a fortress blaze for an alive portal return. Fresh charcoal in the burner below a basin melts three copper ingots plus one tin ingot into 360 mB of CBC bronze; load the ingots before placing the foundry lid. Two separate MI pipes feed a TFMG casting basin: four 90-mB casts yield four bronze ingots, two for the sapper. Use the earlier wheel-making press at 8 RPM, with a depot two blocks below, to turn one TFC steel ingot into one MI steel plate. On a separate 8-RPM drive, point the andesite saw upward and install an Attribute Filter. Sample an earlier andesite shaft and allow only the Added by Greate attribute in whitelist-any mode. Drop the plate onto the saw, then collect all six shafts with an empty hand. For the rubber drive, reduce 8 to 4 to 2 RPM and run one Rubberworks machine at a time. Seven MI pipes and one ordinary Create tank hold the optional 4 L resin batch; keep tank extraction disabled while filling.

Stop the sapper drive by replacing its driving cog with the turning gearbox, leaving the sapper and its tank intact. Feed an east-facing compressor through its west port at positive 2 RPM. Maintain ordinary fire below it using the TFC firestarter. Keep the east-front block clear and put the collector depot one block east and one block down. Enable tank extraction and process the resin in 500 mB batches.

Collect the rubber, disconnect the compressor's input shaft and power the separate andesite press at 2 RPM magnitude. Move the same depot to two blocks below the press, then press one rubber per sheet. The two water-wheel networks stay separate; each has an 8-SU limit.
4C6FD6ECD0FC4D50: Produce the first TFC steel ingot through the industrial-blasting and casting route.
TFMG replaces TFC's blast furnace and the retired MI steam furnace. Supply coke-dust fuel, TFC flux and hot air; handle slag and furnace gas.
The same plant supplies TFC pig iron for native forging. MI's later electric blast furnace remains in progression.

Stack four blast-stove blocks vertically. Each batch combines 50 mB of air and 10 mB of fuel into 50 mB of hot air and 50 mB of carbon dioxide. Start with Railcraft creosote: 44 fuel oak logs yield 11 L for 1,100 batches and 55 L of each output; construction wood is additional. Insert air horizontally at the base and fuel through the top; extract hot air from below and CO2 horizontally. Keep the networks separate and set MI inputs to insert, outputs to extract. For each output, retain the stove’s 32 L storage plus three separate 8 L Create tanks. Furnace gas can fuel the stove after the furnace starts.

For the early intake and stove, make cast-iron fluid tanks with empty wooden barrels, including TFC oak barrels, and the same two cast-iron plates. Craft the stonecutter with three stone blocks, including raw TFC quartzite, and one ordinary iron ingot; use it for the intake’s andesite bars and industrial iron block.

Use a normal three-layer furnace with a side tuyere and top hatch. Drop one iron dust, one TFC flux and three fresh coke dust into an open chute above the top hatch. Draw gas from a side of the hatch so the drop column stays clear. One steel batch consumes 54.4 L of hot air and produces 136 L of furnace gas: reserve eighteen separate 8 L tanks for gas. The CO2 exhaust cannot vent it. Keep 144 mB of slag separate while casting the 144 mB of steel.

Drive one diameter-1 air intake from behind at 64 RPM: an 8-RPM water wheel and three large-to-small cog stages (8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64), joined by andesite-alloy shafts. At steady speed it produces air in 1 mB increments into its 8 L tank. Extract air for the stove; 50 mB feeds one hot-blast batch, while first steel needs the full hot-air budget above.

The TFMG casting line and the Railcraft furnace deliver canonical TFC steel. Independent nonconsuming objectives may count the same sixteen held ingots, including the four-ingot freight task; detection spends none.
047549F249559E07: Craft one MI steel machine casing from four MI steel plates, two precision mechanisms, two nickel ingots and one TFMG steel casing.

For the TFMG casing, fill one TFC oak plank with 250 mB creosote in a spout over a depot. Place the hardened plank, apply one TFC steel ingot, then mine the resulting casing with a correct pickaxe. Application produces a placed block; collect it before crafting.

The steel steam packer uses this casing, three bronze gears, three MI fluid pipes and two MI item pipes. Keep the early heavy-copper-gear/brass-sheet item-pipe recipe. Heat a water- and charcoal-fed bronze boiler and precharge 2,000 mB ordinary steam. A bronze compressor turns three more steel plates into three curved plates at 400 mB steam each; the packer uses 200 mB for four ordinary buckets. These jobs consume 1,400 mB and leave 600 mB before other machine use.

Allow eight new steel ingots after the earlier ignition/shaft pair: five for the casing chain and three for bucket plates. For eight further furnace batches, supply 54.4 L hot air and three additional coke dust per batch, carrying the fuel state. Vent CO₂ through an additional real exhaust. A full furnace-gas hatch can lose gas while steel still completes; discarded gas is unavailable for later use.

Before this first casing, make two additional precision mechanisms with the earlier andesite press and deployer. Complete PRE-01 Precision Mechanisms research; crafting does not wait for the eight-item quest. Keep the original attempt, wrench gold, six saved charcoal and later eight-item batch separate. These two early mechanisms are consumed here.

For two successful attempts, add 38 andesite alloy, four foundry lids, 188 lumber and two earned cold TFC wrought-iron ingots. Craft four batches of eight shafts, 30 small cogs and ten large cogs. The large cogs consume 20 small cogs; the sequence spends the remaining ten small cogs, ten large cogs and ten nuggets over 30 deployments. Use 160 lumber for gear planks and 28 for seven furnace-fuel planks. If one of three attempts fails, instead allow 57 alloy, six lids and 268 lumber; the gold and wrought bill is unchanged. More failures need more inputs, and failure scraps are not part of this bill.

For a separate four-gold batch, add 16 normal native-gold ores, ten clay, eight straw and 18 logs: ten for furnace charcoal and eight for one kiln. Start with two loose granite, three raw granite and four twigs for a fresh hammer, handstone and firestarter; knapping consumes one loose stone. The gold spends 16 hammer uses and 80 handstone uses. Reuse the cleared furnace and cold covered forge. Seven fresh planks smelt the ten charcoal; use all ten charcoal for the earlier four-mold gold schedule and wait for cold molds before pickup. Allow two successful strong ignitions; failed ignition attempts cost extra wear. Two gold sheets feed the two attempts. Keep the two remaining gold ingots, eight nuggets and two shafts separate from later reserves. The two wrought ingots still require their earlier bloomery and forging supplies.

Nickel can precede vanilla buckets. Hammer 16 normal garnierite ores from the earlier gabbro deposits, then use the sluice, quern and second sluice to obtain 80 clean powders. Four fresh molds receive four nickel ingots; allocate two to this first casing and keep two separate. Reuse the cold covered primitive gold forge. Put a new bellows at north (0,1,-1), facing SOUTH toward the forge (0,0,0). Keep its west sky vent (-1,1,0), air above and roof clear. Use manual bellows, disconnected from crank networks; this route needs no nickel compressor, steam or oil bucket.

The additional bill is 16 normal garnierite, 29 oak logs, 82 lumber, ten clay, eight straw, three small sheepskin hides, three loose limestone, two twigs and 3,000 mB fresh water. Knap two new sedimentary knives before crushing the last limestone into two flux. Make three new barrels and one wooden bucket from 24 lumber; six more lumber and the three new leathers make the bellows. The remaining 52 lumber make 13 furnace-fuel planks for 19 new charcoal logs. Eight logs fire four new molds in one kiln; one log makes tannin and one remains the scraping surface. Wait for old furnace fuel to expire and collect actual charcoal; saved charcoal and later tools remain reserved.

Fill each new barrel with 1,000 mB water. Convert one to limewater with both flux, another to tannin with its counted oak log, and keep the third for rinsing. Process all three hides separately through the earlier soaking, scraping, rinsing and tanning route. Each sealed run requires more than 7,200 calendar ticks; one tannin run and nine hide runs leave 100 mB in each barrel. Pay 34 knife uses on the first knife and 17 on the second. The earlier precision hammer, handstone and firestarter pay 16 ore hammer uses, one flux use, 80 quern uses and two successful ignitions, retaining 27/90/4 uses. Spend all 19 charcoal on the existing nickel schedule: 1,000 warmup calls, 16 waves of 1,000 calls with five powders each, bellows every 40 calls, then 4,000 cooling calls with pumping stopped. Keep all four molds in output slots until below 300°C; all may break after extraction. The forge ends cold and without air pressure, ready for the later gold batches.
1872493EE179B692: Build a Railcraft Item Loader and install it beside a serviced freight track and cargo cart.
Transfer a real production batch through the loader, then document the destination and the manual recovery path before expanding the corridor.

Operate a Create portable storage interface on the serviced train route; its native advancement records an actual interface connection. Railcraft loading and unloading handles the mature terminal. Route throughput and unattended recovery still need an operating check.

Each item loader and unloader needs an item detector: craft eight stripped wood blocks around one stone pressure plate. Use full stripped wood blocks and stone pressure plates; TFC variants of both are accepted. Supply the rail-grade steel plates, standard rails and controller circuits for both terminal machines through their existing production lines.

Each Railcraft controller circuit uses one repeater, two red wool blocks, one slime ball, one gold ingot, one lapis gem and two redstone dust. Ordinary slime balls match the installed common tag; TFC lapis gems match the lapis tag. Reserve four circuits for the selected locomotive, loader, unloader and advanced-loader crafts.

Look for Beneath's slimed netherrack in the Nether and return alive with 13 raw slime. The quern makes 13 ordinary slime balls: reserve four for circuits and craft nine into a slime block, then nine TFC glue. One glue, paper, flux, sand and gem powder make sandpaper. Mine four TFC lapis ores in limestone or marble (Y -20 to 80) and polish them; four crafts use four of a fresh sandpaper's 40 durability. One panned amethyst ore gives four gem powders in the quern, with only one needed here. Prepare the expedition's tools before departure; this extra glue batch supplies the later sandpaper.

Spin eight TFC wool into 64 yarn, weave four cloth, then eight white wool. The MI bronze mixer dyes all eight with one red dye for 200 mB steam; use the rail-stock packet's last clean hematite powder for that dye. Add a mixer and two steam pipes; the mixer craft also consumes two pipes. An additional 2,000 mB charge from the existing boiler leaves 1,800 mB after this job; keep earlier machine residues separate and supply water, heat and fuel. Reserve four gold ingots and 20 redstone dust for the four repeaters and final circuit crafts.

Mine 16 normal native-gold ores from TFC igneous rock veins (Y 0 to 70). Hammer them into 80 rocky chunks, wash those in the sluice, quern the 80 gold chunks, then wash all 80 dirty powders. Each clean gold powder melts into five TFC metal units at 1,060 °C: the 400 units supply exactly four gold ingots. Allow 16 additional hammer uses and 80 handstone uses; optional washing drops do not count toward this batch.

Use a separate charcoal forge for these four gold ingots. Knap four fresh ingot molds from 10 additional clay balls and fire them together with eight oak logs and eight straw; let the fired pottery cool for 4000 player ticks before pickup. Build an eight-charcoal pile with five additional raw-granite insulation blocks at the four sides and below. Use one of the two spare blast-furnace bricks temporarily above the pile to place the other brick two blocks above it as a rain cover. Recover the temporary brick before lighting; keep the space directly above the forge empty and a neighboring sky column open. One spare brick remains. Reserve 23 charcoal from the earlier coking byproducts while preserving the 550-charcoal rail-furnace reserve: eight build the forge, ten fuel it and five stay spare. For a cold forge, warm for 1500 ticks, then process sixteen loads of five powders for up to 1000 ticks each, with four fresh molds in the mold output slots. The covered forge reaches 1350°C without bellows, above gold’s 1060°C melt; rain without the cover lowers it too far. After all four molds fill, stop feeding fuel and leave them in the unheated output slots for 4000 player ticks before collecting. Pickup must be below 300°C because TFCHotOrNot can eject hot items. Extract four cold ingots and assume all molds break. No hot vessel transfer or later nickel equipment is needed; reserve all four ingots for the circuits. Extra delays and the other factories’ fuel remain additional.

For two item detectors, craft 24 additional oak logs into 18 full wood blocks. Place 16, strip them with a fresh sedimentary stone axe, then recover them with that axe; keep the other two full wood blocks. The 16 stripping actions and 16 recoveries use 32 of the axe’s 50 durability, leaving 18. Obtain the 24 actual logs separately and allow additional forestry wear. Four ordinary raw-granite mining drops provide at least four loose granite rocks (one to four per drop). Chisel four bricks, then two stone pressure plates; these six crafts use six chisel durability. Each detector consumes eight recovered full stripped wood blocks and one plate.

Prepare a new copper chisel from a forged head, copper rivet, glue and a stick handle. Two additional TFC copper ingots supply one head and the rod-to-stamen-to-rivet line; keep one spare rod, one stamen and four rivets. Use one of the input packet’s eight spare glues, leaving seven. One further stick makes the fresh axe; rock knapping requires two sedimentary loose rocks in hand and consumes one. Work at the Copper anvil with a stone hammer and workable-temperature feed. A fresh 600-durability copper chisel retains 594 after the brick and plate crafts. Budget forging-hammer wear and working heat separately.

For the four controllers, mine three cinnabar ores with a bronze pick or better. Look in gneiss, phyllite, quartzite or schist: deep veins occur below Y 10, with mountain veins at Y 120–280. Each ore gives seven rocky chunks under the hammer. Sluice all 21, quern the resulting chunks, then sluice the dirty dust into 21 ordinary redstone dust. Use a fresh intrusive stone hammer and handstone: three hammer crafts leave 57 of 60 durability, and 21 quern jobs leave 229 of 250. The earlier workshop’s redstone and tool costs remain additional.

Collect 15 raw granite blocks by exposing all six faces and allowing TFC to drop the isolated block: reserve 12 for repeaters and three for the new handstone. Obtain two loose granite rocks for the new hammer’s knapping threshold; one is consumed. The enabled utility craft turns two additional oak logs into 16 sticks: spend one on each tool and eight on torches, leaving six. Allocate the 21 dust once: eight for eight torches, four for four repeaters, and eight directly for four circuits, leaving one dust. The circuits also consume the reserved four gold ingots, four lapis gems, four slime balls and eight red wool. Keep both detectors for the terminal crafts.

For the two hoppers, make five additional steel ingots; the earlier forty are already allocated. Twenty more normal hematite ores become 100 clean powders and 25 pellets: five briquets plus five separate pellets supply five 100-unit blooms and five wrought ingots. Mill those ingots with a new 2000 mB steam charge, then add five flux for steelmaking. Allow at least 125 mB more boiler water plus heating fuel and additional forging-tool wear. Twelve new bituminous coal become twelve coke dust: add these to the retained furnace fuel unit at timer 400. Eleven dust would leave the fifth batch unable to complete. Coke 218 more actual oak logs for 54,500 mB creosote; with the prior 60 mB, spend 54,400 mB on the five hot-air replenishments, leaving 160 mB. Ten of the new charcoal byproducts fuel the five blooms. Reuse 20 hammer and 100 handstone uses from the circuit packet, leaving 37 and 129 respectively.

Press the five new steel ingots into five ordinary MI steel plates at the existing independent 8 RPM, 8 SU tier-0 depot press. The MI hand recipe turns eight further oak logs into four ordinary chests; use one chest and all five plates for two hoppers, retaining three chests. These eight logs are additional to the 218 fuel logs. Keep the existing typed slag line: the five batches raise stored slag from 5760 to 6480 mB in its 8000 mB tank. The full furnace-gas bank retains none of the additional gas. Craft and detect the base item loader before upgrading it. The loader, unloader and upgrade together consume both hoppers, both detectors, three circuits, twelve rail plates, six standard rails and the crowbar. Finish with one advanced loader and one unloader; the base loader has been consumed. Keep one circuit, one plate, one standard rail, one track part and the underframe for the still-unfinished locomotive.
2F33DA300848472E: Roll the coke-brick, steel-plate, rail, and minecart underframe in Railcraft before moving it to the Create line.

Run the underframe through the eleven deployment steps for the firebox, boiler, steel mechanism, running gear, control circuit, steel plate, tank, pump, controls and pipework. Fill the workpiece with 250 mB of TFMG lubrication oil, then finish it on a Steel Greate Press or higher.
This nonconsuming freight task counts four of the sixteen reserved canonical TFC steel ingots. Keep all sixteen; no additional four-ingot batch is needed.

Mechanical commissioning: finish the locomotive on a Steel Greate Press or higher, supplied by the steel and lubricant district. Commission the loader, unloader and fuel service as part of the freight route.

The manual rolling machine consumes three entry mechanical presses, four heavy bronze gears, one coke oven brick and one andesite casing. An early diagonal pattern of three bronze ingots produces four rebar. Keep the menu open. With only one item per occupied slot, click the recipe preview with an empty cursor to permit the final batch, then collect the completed parts from the output slot. Rail-grade steel rolling still needs its own materials and research.

Build a 3×4×3 Railcraft blast furnace from 34 furnace-brick blocks, leaving air in the center of each of the two middle layers. Nine brick crafts make 36 blocks, leaving two spare. Feed newly produced TFMG steel and ordinary charcoal, and keep both output slots free: one TFC steel ingot yields one TFC steel ingot and one slag. This nonconsuming freight task counts four of the sixteen reserved canonical TFC steel ingots. Keep all sixteen; no additional four-ingot batch is needed.

For the selected locomotive and terminal parts, plan four plate batches (16 MI steel plates), one standard-rail batch (16 rails) and one track-part batch (three parts: two for the rails, one for the locomotive). The plate and rail rolls use 22 rail-grade steel ingots. The underframe takes two coke-oven bricks, two plates, two standard rails and a minecart. Pack that cart in the MI steam packer from one large steel plate (four new canonical steel plates) and one ordinary Minecraft rail, using 200 mB steam. Use TFMG nuggets for track parts. The crowbar takes three more TFC steel ingots and four red dyes; process one extra normal hematite with the hammer, sluice, quern and sluice again for enough clean pigment.

Before bulk TFMG steel production, cast the current ingot and empty the primary steel tank. Then connect a separate, initially blank MI pipe network from the output block to a newly built ordinary Create fluid tank, so it selects molten slag. Keep this network separate from steel. Forty steel batches make 5,760 mB slag, which fits one 8,000 mB tank; without extraction, the furnace's slag tank blocks batch 28.

Use the Greate andesite-alloy mechanical pump for the pump deployment. The pack’s shared entry-pump tag accepts it. Build one pump from three of the six retained andesite shafts, nine new andesite alloy, one new oak log, four new oak lumber, three new TFC copper ingots and one fresh basin foundry lid. Press two copper ingots into plates; the third ingot, both plates and lid make four fluid pipes. Use one pipe for the pump and keep three. One alloy, one shaft and the plank make its cog; eight alloy and the log make its casing. Three retained shafts remain. Use fresh materials for this bill; keep the drive intact.

The pump bill keeps five precision mechanisms, eight steel mechanisms, sixteen objective TFC steel ingots and the additional MI casing. Controls still need one precision mechanism, a lever and a railway casing. That casing uses a brass casing and a sturdy sheet; fund the obsidian powder, lava and pressing sequence for the sheet. The firebox, boiler, tank, cast-iron pipe and 250 mB oil delivery also need their own inputs. This nonconsuming freight task counts four of the sixteen reserved canonical TFC steel ingots. Keep all sixteen; no additional four-ingot batch is needed.

TFC’s native lava springs provide a terrestrial source: underground placements sample Y −64 to 63, and surface placements Y 64 to 220. Search the native rock terrain for an actual source block; placement attempts do not guarantee a spring. A flowing lava stream alone is not a valid pump intake. Establish the pump drive, intake and fluid receiver before counting collected lava. The heated Rubberworks obsidian craft takes 1000 mB, and the sturdy-sheet route uses another 500 mB. Keep this lava handling separate from the oil district.

After stopping the drive and emptying the intake buffers and pipes, use the retained Create wrench to recover the andesite-alloy shaft, small cog and mechanical pump. Sneak-right-click returns the corresponding part in normal survival; keep room in your inventory. Reuse these parts at the next source or recover the pump for locomotive assembly. Leave filled lava receivers in place: recovering the kinetic parts does not carry hot tank contents with them.

For two separate lava receivers, add 3 andesite alloy, 2 foundry lids, 46 oak lumber and 4 TFC copper ingots; press the copper into four plates on the existing steel press. Craft eight shafts, one water wheel, one small cog and two tanks. Keep the three older shafts. At each isolated source use the paid pump and two retained fluid pipes. With all axes X, place the wheel at (-5,1,0), four shafts through (-1,1,0), cog at (0,1,0), pump facing EAST at (0,0,0), intake pipe at (-1,0,0), source at (-2,0,0), output pipe at (1,0,0) and tank at (2,0,0). Translate the whole layout to the site. A sustained contained freshwater current drives only this rig; keep it away from lava. Wait for 1000 mB in tank A and an empty intake, stop and recover the rig, then repeat at source B with its own tank. Leave both tanks placed. Recover the pump for the locomotive; six new shafts and all three pipes remain. No obsidian or sturdy sheet is made yet.

For obsidian at receiver A, add 16 andesite alloy, one foundry lid, 28 oak lumber and one oak log. Combine the three older and six recently recovered andesite shafts with one new eight-shaft batch; make five new small cogs, two large cogs and one depot. After the earlier jobs finish, stop and wrench the empty Rubberworks compressor and the captured burner after its old fuel expires. Keep tank A at (2,0,0), put the pump facing EAST at (3,0,0), and the compressor facing EAST at (4,0,0). Extend the capture wheel’s axis-X drive to seven shafts and a cog above the pump. Keep the compressor unpowered while the pump transfers all 1000 mB into its west inlet. Stop and recover the feed drive and pump before compression.

Use the recovered wheel with two small-to-large gear reductions and an axis-Z shaft drive to run only the compressor at 2 RPM, using all 8 SU. Put the captured burner directly below it, a depot forward and one block lower, and keep the forward cell clear. Prepare the lava, drive and collector before spending one charcoal for KINDLED heat; passive fire is insufficient. Collect the obsidian and carry it as an item to the bronze macerator; clear its input and output slots first: 200 mB steam guarantees one powdered obsidian. Do not budget the optional 75% obsidian return. Return the empty compressor and cooled burner to their earlier stations. Keep receiver B’s 1000 mB reserved. After recovering the wheel, shafts and small cogs, hold twelve andesite shafts, two small cogs, one wheel, one pump and three pipes; leave the two large cogs and empty new depot at A. Macerator steam falls from 800 to 600 mB, and the 190 charcoal reserve falls to 189 before other heat uses.

For the sturdy sheet, recover the earlier empty oil spout and its empty depot with the wrench; first clear their items and confirm the oil tank, pipes and spout are empty. At receiver B, keep the tank at (2,0,0), face the pump EAST at (3,0,0), and put the spout at (4,0,0) with its depot at (4,-2,0). Reuse the wheel, cog and seven-shaft X drive. Transfer all 1000 mB into the spout, then stop the pump. Place one powdered obsidian on the depot and wait for its 500 mB filling to complete. Empty-hand use on the depot’s top collects the same marked workpiece. Isolate the drive, re-place the empty pump facing WEST, and return the remaining 500 mB to receiver B. Stop and recover the rig only after the spout is empty; return the empty earlier spout and depot to their factory positions.

Carry the same marked workpiece to the existing supported steel press and complete two pressings at 1 RPM. Keep its sequence component intact between operations; an unmarked transitional item cannot replace it. This native sequence has one loop: one powder, one 500 mB filling and two pressings produce one sturdy sheet. Reserve that sheet for the railway casing and controls. Wrench the now-empty receiver A and reserve its Create fluid tank for the locomotive. Keep receiver B placed with 500 mB lava. After recovery retain twelve andesite shafts, two small cogs, one wheel, one pump and all three pipes. This step needs no further steam, charcoal or raw-material crafting; the earlier spout, depot and steel press remain available at the factory.

Make the controls lever with fresh terrestrial materials: arrange four loose granite rocks in a 2x2 square to craft one TFC granite cobblestone, then put one oak twig above that cobblestone in the player crafting grid. The recipe accepts normal TFC cobblestones and twigs, along with ordinary Minecraft cobblestone and stick, and produces one lever. Reserve the lever for controls. These two crafts use no machine, steam, fuel or tool and leave the sturdy sheet, empty locomotive tank, pump and five precision mechanisms untouched. The foundry-brass casing and its recovery still need to be supplied before assembling controls.

For the controls, finish Brass Engineering and bring six new cold TFC copper ingots, one TFC zinc ingot, two Create andesite alloy, four TFC fire-brick blocks and one actual oak log. Use the earlier 3x3 crafting service: three copper across the top, alloy on both sides of one masonry block in the middle, and three masonry blocks across the bottom make one new foundry lid. Reuse the existing heated andesite mixer, basin and captured burner with its supported 8 RPM drive, 4 SU load and 8 SU capacity; leave the portable rig reserved. Keep the basin facing DOWN, empty its input/output slots and disconnect external item extraction. Drop the remaining three copper ingots, zinc ingot and new lid into the basin and check that all five items entered. When the inputs, fresh-water drive and mixer are ready, feed one retained charcoal to the burner. This batch makes four Create brass ingots and returns the lid. Stop the drive after the batch; collect both output stacks with an empty hand and leave the basin empty. The charcoal reserve falls from 189 to 188 before other open uses; do not count leftover burner heat as fresh fuel.

Place the new oak log and strip it with the retained sedimentary axe, reducing its remaining uses from 18 to 17. Apply one of the four Create brass ingots to that stripped log for a placed brass casing, then apply the paid sturdy sheet to the same casing for a placed railway casing. Keep inventory space and sneak-use the paid wrench to recover this final casing where block breaking is allowed. In the earlier 3x3 crafting table, put the paid lever above the railway casing and one of the five held precision mechanisms below it. Reserve the resulting controls for the locomotive. The sheet, lever and railway casing are consumed; retain four precision mechanisms, three brass ingots and the returned new lid. Keep the empty locomotive tank, pump, portable rig, eight steel mechanisms, sixteen separate objective TFC steel ingots, additional MI casing and earlier steam reservations untouched. The locomotive still needs its remaining parts, 250 mB oil and final assembly.

For one locomotive firebox, collect eleven new whole granite blocks and three new oak twigs. Whole granite requires clearing all six neighboring collision faces and letting isolation release the block; ordinary direct mining gives loose rocks instead. Find one saltpeter ore in chalk at Y40–100 and one sulfur ore in tuff at Y40–200, using a bronze pickaxe or better. Suitable regional rock, access and additional excavation/tool wear still need to be supplied. Bring back seven additional whole netherrack through the same isolation method and an alive Nether return. Craft a new furnace from eight granite, a new handstone from the other three granite and one twig, and a new firestarter from the other two twigs. Keep this new furnace held for the firebox; use the earlier placed furnace and quern as processing services, preserving their existing tools and other reserved locomotive stock.

Insert the new handstone into the existing manual quern. Grind the saltpeter ore, sulfur ore and one retained charcoal separately; turn the handle and collect each batch of four powder before loading the next. Remove the new handstone afterwards with 247 uses left. Craft two saltpeter powder, one sulfur powder and one charcoal powder into four gunpowder. One gunpowder, one further charcoal and the entire new firestarter make one fire charge; this craft consumes the firestarter, so do not spend the workshop ignition tool. Load all seven netherrack into the empty earlier furnace and use one further charcoal to smelt seven nether bricks, keeping output room clear. On the 3x3 table, put three bricks across the top, brick/charge/brick in the middle and brick/new furnace/brick at the bottom. Reserve the resulting firebox. The three charcoal uses reduce the reserve from 188 to 185 before other open uses; retain three gunpowder, two saltpeter powder, three sulfur powder, three charcoal powder and the new handstone. Controls, empty tank, pump, precision and steel reservations stay intact. The boiler, cast-iron pipe, oil and final locomotive assembly remain.

Make the locomotive boiler’s four copper rings from four additional cold TFC copper ingots. Reuse the retained press above its empty depot on the supported 1 RPM drive, with 6 SU load under 8 SU capacity, and disconnect external item extraction. Load one ingot, press it into a flat Create copper sheet and collect it. Reinsert that sheet, press it into an MI copper curved plate and collect it. Reinsert the curved plate, press it into one copper ring and collect it. After each completed pressing, sneak-use the paid wrench to recover the existing press-side input shaft and pause the drive. Transfer the item, then replace that same shaft; keep the depot clear between items. Repeat for all four ingots: twelve single-item pressings make four rings, with one copper ingot spent per ring and no flat or curved plates left over. Reserve all four rings for the new bronze tank used in the locomotive boiler. This work uses no steam, fuel or tool wear; retain 185 charcoal before other open uses, 600 mB macerator steam, the firebox, controls, empty locomotive tank, pump and earlier steel/component stocks. The boiler’s other parts still need their own supplies.

Supply four TFC brass sheets for the spare boiler’s glass apparatus. Add six cold TFC copper ingots, two zinc ingots, thirteen oak twigs, three loose limestone and three loose granite. Use the returned lid in two further heated brass batches on the existing mixer: spend one charcoal per batch and collect eight new Create brass ingots plus the returned lid. Preserve the three older brass ingots and four copper rings. Knap a new sedimentary knife and two intrusive stone hammers; each knap needs at least two loose rocks and consumes one. Use the two remaining limestone in two hammer crafts for four flux. The thirteen twigs cover the knife, two hammers, four wooden tongs and one new firestarter. Craft the tongs with the new knife; keep the workshop tools intact.

Process four separate pairs in the earlier sheltered gold forge beside the Copper anvil. Each pair gets exactly two charcoal: warm the empty forge for 1500 ticks, then heat the two ingots for 1200 ticks. Keep fresh wooden tongs held throughout the hot transfer; move both ingots into the anvil and sneak-use a hammer to weld them with one flux within 80 player ticks of the first pickup. Complete the sheet plan within 120 ticks, matching its target and ending with three light hits; every target has a sequence of at most twelve steps. Leave the sheet in the anvil for 7000 player ticks before cold pickup. Let the forge burn out and cool between pairs. Four successful first-attempt relights use four firestarter charges; failed attempts need extra tool allocation. Both mixes and four forge pairs spend ten charcoal, leaving 175 before other open uses. Reserve all four sheets for the glass apparatus; the glass, boiler and remaining locomotive work are still unfinished.

For the glass batch, bring 32 new cold recovered oak logs, eight straw, ten clay balls, two loose limestone, two oak twigs and one white sand. Knap a new sedimentary axe; one limestone and one twig make its head and handle. Strip and recover 24 placed logs with this axe, spending 48 uses; keep eight logs for a pit kiln. Use the existing upward andesite saw alone on its independent 8 RPM/8 SU drive, with empty fluid tank and output filter. Feed one stripped log at a time, collect every completed job and stop when three oak supports appear; cannon moulds can precede them. Cut two supports into eight lumber. Four lumber make one plank; the other four and one twig make a paddle. The four reserved TFC brass sheets, plank and hammer make eight brass blocks: five for an air-centered basin, one isolated pouring table and two spares. Hammer the remaining limestone into two flux. Knap two unfired ceramic pipes from the ten clay balls; fire both pipes and one flux together in the eight-log/eight-straw pit kiln, then recover two bare pipes and one lime.

Combine one retained saltpeter powder, the lime and white sand into four silica glass batches. Load two separate ceramic pipes and retain two batches. In the cold sheltered forge, use one charcoal: warm the empty forge for 800 ticks, then heat both loaded pipes in separate slots for 310 ticks. Keep the glass tool held throughout each transfer and pour, allowing at most 80 player ticks including use. Pour the first pipe into the brass basin, wait 102 cooling ticks and recover one glass block. Keep the second pipe heating during that wait; then table-pour it, flatten immediately with the paddle and wait 62 cooling ticks before ordinary recovery of one glass pane. Both pipes may break after successful pours; their return is not needed. Let the forge burn out and cool. Reserve both glass outputs for the separate boiler bill; retain 174 charcoal before other open uses, one saltpeter powder, one flux, two spare brass blocks, one support and the paddle. The new axe retains at least two uses, the first sheet hammer 32 and the sheet firestarter two after successful first-attempt kiln/forge ignitions. Other reserved stock stays intact; the boiler, oil, cast-iron pipe and final locomotive assembly still need completion.

For the separate locomotive boiler, bring 37 new cold TFC copper ingots, five tin ingots, eight whole granite, eight clay balls and one recovered oak log. Reuse the earlier bronze-only foundry line in place, including its lid, basin, two MI pipes, caster, chute and captured burner. Run five batches of three copper plus one tin: one charcoal per batch melts 360 mB bronze for four cold CBC ingots. Clear each batch and let the burner expire before starting the next. Press the twenty ingots into twenty MI bronze plates; turn six plates into six bronze curved plates. Six other copper ingots supply six flat sheets and then six MI copper curved plates; press two curves into two new rings. Use the existing paused 1 RPM/6 SU press under 8 SU capacity: forty single-item pressings in total, pausing the input shaft with the paid wrench before each collection as above. On the independent upward saw with empty tank and filter, feed single copper ingots until you collect a copper rod, at most eleven jobs in the reviewed cycle. Set the output filter with that actual rod and process five further ingots, then clear the filter with an empty hand. The rod used as the ordinary selector remains yours. Use four copper curves and two rods for eight blades, and cut the other four rods into eight bolts. The blades, bolts and two new rings make two rotors; keep the four older rings for the tank.

Six bronze curves, the two new rotors and the reserved pane make twelve MI fluid pipes. Use two in the boiler and retain ten. Four bronze plates, the four older rings and the reserved glass block make its new tank. Strip the new log with the glass-batch axe, apply one of the three held Create brass ingots, then sneak-wrench the brass casing into inventory where breaking is allowed and space is clear. Use it with eight bronze plates for the new bronze machine casing. In the old empty furnace, smelt four clay balls into four ordinary bricks with one charcoal and let that fuel burn out. Two unheated mixer batches, each with two bricks and two further clay balls, make eight fire-clay dust. Load all eight dust and one fresh charcoal together into the old furnace; its automatic batch makes eight fire-clay bricks. Craft two blocks from four bricks each. Craft a new furnace from the eight whole granite and keep it for the boiler. Combine the two remaining bronze plates, tank, two new MI pipes, two fire-clay blocks, new furnace and new casing into one additional bronze boiler. The seven charcoal for this whole bill leave 167 before other open uses; retain two Create brass, ten MI pipes and at least one use on the glass-batch axe. The working steam plant, controls, firebox, empty locomotive tank, pump, steel and other reserves stay intact. The cast-iron pipe, oil and final locomotive assembly remain.

For the separate cast-iron pipe batch, bring three additional cold TFC cast-iron ingots. On the retained steel press over its empty depot, use the same 1 RPM/6 SU drive under 8 SU capacity. Press two ingots separately into two TFMG cast-iron sheets. Pause the input shaft with the paid wrench before each collection and keep external extraction disconnected. TFC anvil cast-iron sheets do not fit this recipe. Craft the two new TFMG sheets with the third cast-iron ingot into four cast-iron pipes, using either the horizontal or vertical recipe. Hold all four: reserve one for the locomotive and leave three spare. This batch uses no charcoal or steam; keep 167 charcoal before other open uses, the additional bronze boiler, ten MI pipes and all other reserved components. The locomotive still needs its oil, remaining assembly inputs and locomotive-systems research.

After both earlier nonconsuming oil-bucket objectives have registered, reuse one of the two filled TFMG oil buckets. The six litres used for steel mechanisms are already spent. At the existing oil station, use the paid wrench to remove one input shaft from the bridge mixer’s drive where breaking is allowed; keep the shaft and stop the mixer. Keep the basin facing down and begin with its input/output tanks, buffer, all transfer pipes and spout empty. Close both endpoints of the lubricant feed, basin extraction and tank-to-spout branches. With room in inventory, normally use one held filled oil bucket on the basin. The complete 1,000 mB enters the basin and the empty vanilla bucket returns to you. Direct bucket use on the spout is not needed.

Open only the existing basin-to-buffer branch. Wait until both basin storages and its two MI pipe buffers are empty and the ordinary buffer holds all 1,000 mB of TFMG oil; close that branch. Open only the buffer-to-spout branch, wait for the buffer and both pipes to empty into the spout, then close both endpoints. Replace the retained mixer shaft. Hold 1,000 mB in the spout, one filled oil bucket and three empty vanilla buckets. Reserve 250 mB for the correctly marked locomotive frame at its later filling step after locomotive-systems research; that future fill leaves 750 mB. This handoff needs no new pump, pipes, tank, fuel or steam. Keep the additional boiler, four cast-iron pipes, ten MI pipes, 167 charcoal before other open uses and all other components reserved. Check the earlier reserved frame, rail, circuit, plate and track part before completing the final sequence.

Once Locomotive Systems is unlocked and the nonconsuming eight-steel-mechanism objective has registered, use the five parts reserved by the rail-terminal bill: one frame, standard rail, controller circuit, steel plate and track part. Use the existing downward USE deployer, spout, depots and steel press on the 1 RPM/6 SU forming drive under 8 SU capacity. Process one frame at a time and load one real component for each deployment. Apply these eleven parts in order: solid-fueled firebox, additional held bronze boiler, steel mechanism, standard rail, controller circuit, reserved steel plate, track part, empty Create fluid tank, paid Greate andesite pump, controls and cast-iron pipe. Use the actual reserved MI or Railcraft steel plate. Keep the same partially assembled frame and its progress through every move; pause the input shaft with the paid wrench before collecting it.

After all eleven deployments, put that marked frame under the isolated oil spout for one 250 mB fill. Its 1,000 mB falls to 750 mB. Then perform one tier-one pressing on the existing steel press. This completes the single thirteen-action loop and gives one finished steam locomotive with no unfinished-sequence marker. Keep it in inventory for detection. The bill consumes the five named rail reservations, the additional boiler and other deployed parts, one of eight mechanisms, one of four cast-iron pipes and 250 mB oil. Retain seven mechanisms, three cast-iron pipes, ten MI pipes, one filled oil bucket, three empty buckets, 167 charcoal before other open uses and sixteen separate objective TFC steel ingots. Keep the working steam plant placed. No new fuel, steam or hardware is needed for this assembly. This nonconsuming freight task counts four of the sixteen reserved canonical TFC steel ingots. Keep all sixteen; no additional four-ingot batch is needed.

The TFMG casting line and the Railcraft furnace deliver canonical TFC steel. Independent nonconsuming objectives may count the same sixteen held ingots, including the four-ingot freight task; detection spends none.

Before registering freight, confirm both parent milestones: sixteen canonical MI steel plates were held before spending them on rail parts, and eight steel mechanisms were detected before one entered the locomotive. The seven remaining mechanisms cannot complete the eight-item parent retroactively.

Close the manual rolling-machine menu while alive with room for its returned inputs and real output. Preserve those leftovers, then recover the empty machine with an ordinary empty-hand survival break where breaking and drops are allowed. Hold that one machine, the finished unmarked locomotive and all sixteen TFC ingots in main inventory, with an empty cursor. Wait for actual quest detection, then place the same machine back to restore rolling service. Recovery and replacement create no extra machine and spend no steel, fuel, steam or mining-tool durability.
41F95A6E5A884B05: Collect eight finished TFMG steel mechanisms together before spending them on later builds. Each attempt starts with one heavy plate. On the same workpiece, apply a steel casing, fill with 250 mB TFMG lubrication oil, apply a nickel plate, apply a lead plate, then press at tier 1 or higher. Repeat this five-step loop three times while preserving the sequence marker. A complete attempt consumes three casings, three nickel plates, three lead plates and 750 mB oil, with nine deployments, three fillings and three pressings.

The completed attempt selects one result with weights 120 for a mechanism, 4 for a heavy plate and 2 for a steel ingot. The mechanism has a nominal 20-in-21 share; it is not guaranteed. Failed attempts still consume all deployed parts and oil. Returned plate or ingot does not refund them. Keep supplying attempts until eight mechanisms are collected; eight attempts are only enough if all eight succeed. The later batch recipe needs an existing mechanism as its retained catalyst and cannot create the first one.

The native heavy-plate sequence starts with one steel ingot and performs three ordinary pressing steps; its omitted loop count defaults to one. Greate presses accept these Create sequence steps, while the mechanism’s final step still requires tier 1. One independent 8 RPM, 8 SU source with three small-to-large cog reductions gives 1 RPM: the steel press and deployer together use 6 SU, leaving 2 SU spare under the andesite limit. Use a downward-facing deployer in USE mode and depots two blocks below the processors; move the marked workpiece between depots in order. All hardware and extra input stocks still need to be made.

Lead for eight successful attempts follows the graded galena line: 108 additional normal ores -> 216 crushed raw lead -> 216 guaranteed MI tiny dust -> 24 dust -> 24 smelted ingots -> 24 MI lead plates. Use the existing tier-0 paired crushing wheels, then wash on a depot one block ahead and one below an andesite fan; keep the air in front clear and choose rotation that blows toward the depot. Fill the fan’s internal tank with ordinary water and select circuit 0. Native washing spends 1 mB per item: 216 mB for this branch; a 1000 mB charge leaves 784 mB. At 8 RPM the fan loads 4 SU on its own 8 SU source. Supply the additional ore, fan parts, water, furnace fuel and 9600 mB compressor steam. Optional silver is extra; failed mechanism attempts require replacement parts and oil.

For this 24-plate batch, add 20 andesite alloy, two foundry lids, 32 oak lumber and one TFC tin ingot. Use the two spare full-oak-wood blocks from the detector batch for two casings; stripping is unnecessary. Make eight planks and eight shafts: the wheel, cog and fan consume four shafts, leaving four to install. Make the fan tin plate first in the bronze compressor. Borrow one of the two empty buckets, fill the fan with one ordinary water source and recover the bucket; keep both oil buckets untouched. Place one spare terminal chest and reserve 24 slots. Smelt one lead dust at a time in the existing empty furnace with four charcoal from the additional steel batch; collect and reload within 60 furnace ticks after each completion, or supply more fuel. From the compressor’s separate 400 mB reserve, spend 200 on tin, add 7600, compress 19 lead ingots, add 2000 and compress five more: 200 mB remains. The new 9600 mB steam needs at least 600 mB additional boiler water plus heating fuel; keep it separate from the fan water and other machines’ reserves. Hold all 24 lead plates. The earlier workshop inputs, boiler operation, nickel, oil and remaining forming hardware still need provisioning.

For nickel, hammer 96 additional normal garnierite ores, then use the existing TFC sluice, quern and sluice again to obtain 480 clean powders. Supply one new hammer, two handstones and a bellows. Make 24 fresh ingot molds from 60 clay balls; six kiln loads of four molds consume 48 logs and 48 straw. Let the fired pottery cool before pickup. Build an eight-charcoal forge pile with stone insulation on four sides and below; keep air and sky above. Put the bellows one block above and beside the forge, facing toward it. Plain charcoal reaches only 1350°C; bellows are required for nickel’s 1453°C melt. Use six groups of four molds in the forge’s mold output slots. Per group, supply 19 charcoal, warm for 1000 forge ticks, then heat sixteen five-powder loads for up to 1000 ticks each while pumping every 40 game ticks. Stop fueling and pumping, leave the four full molds in the unheated output slots for 4000 player ticks, then collect them below 300°C; TFCHotOrNot can eject hotter items. Reserve 119 fuel charcoal plus eight for construction; the selected schedule burns 114 fuel items and leaves five spares, with more needed for delays. Assume every mold breaks after extraction. Use the second spare terminal chest and keep the 24 lead plates untouched. Compress the 24 nickel ingots with 9600 mB of new steam: add 7600 to the old 200 reserve, run 19 jobs, add 2000 and run five; 200 remains. Supply at least 600 mB of additional boiler water and heating fuel. Oil and the remaining forming equipment are still required. For the corrected earlier tool budget, this nickel batch uses 36 of the old hammer’s 37 uses, 59 on its new 60-use hammer and one on the steel workshop’s retained 25-use fourth hammer. They retain 1/1/24 uses; the other three one-use steel hammers remain untouched.

For an additional 6000 mB oil, reuse the separate earlier oil station and its 17 pipes. Preserve the two filled oil buckets and two empty buckets. Supply 24 new oak logs and 12 redstone: the Railcraft coke oven makes 6000 mB creosote and 24 charcoal; collect each charcoal output and hold it unallocated. Twelve bronze-mixer jobs consume the creosote and make 6000 mB MI lubricant. Spend the oil circuit’s old 1200 mB steam once on the first six jobs, then supply 1200 mB new steam for the other six. The new steam needs at least 75 mB additional boiler water plus heating fuel and actual delivery. Preserve the separate compressor 200, macerator 2800 and textile mixer 1800 mB reserves, and all reserved steel, planks, shafts and plates.

Clear the old depot and close the tank-to-spout line during production. Keep basin extraction closed while feeding only two mixer jobs per batch. Wait until their full 1000 mB lubricant reaches basin input and the mixer output and feed pipes are empty. Run the existing ambient bridge once; only after basin input is empty, extract the TFMG oil and drain both output pipes completely into the 8 L tank. Repeat six times, holding all 6000 mB in the tank with process pipes and spout empty. Reopening the two-pipe spout line can leave oil in the pipes; count tank, pipes and spout together. Twenty-four matching 250 mB mechanism fillings can then consume the 6000 mB, conditional on the remaining hardware and marked workpieces. Eight successful attempts, extra stocks for failures and the earlier aggregate workshop supply still need qualification.

For the steel press, use the separately reserved 37 TFC steel ingots, 25 hardened planks and two steel shafts. After Precision Mechanisms and Steel Mechanisms research, keep the early andesite press working long enough to make four canonical steel plates and eight heavy plates; the heavy plates need 24 pressing steps in total. One more steel ingot and one hardened plank make the press casing. Add four new andesite alloy, one foundry lid and eight lumber: make two planks, one eight-shaft batch and two new small andesite cogs. With the one shaft spare left after the wrench, seven andesite shafts remain. Upgrade these two new cogs using the two reserved STEEL shafts and two of the four plates. The two remaining plates, casing, earlier andesite press and one successful precision mechanism craft the steel press. This leaves 24 steel ingots and 24 hardened planks for the remaining mechanism casings; the eight heavy plates are held separately. Preserve the sixteen objective ingots, lead, nickel and oil reserves.

Prepare and collect all pressed parts before dismantling the early press. A failed precision attempt supplies no precision mechanism: retain the early press and prepared construction parts, and fund another attempt. The wrench used the three spare gold ingots; after collecting any byproduct, replenish each missing gold sheet, cog and nugget for the next attempt. Keep the three installed drive cogs and the attempt cogs separate from these two new press cogs. Before spending one precision mechanism on the press, hold eight finished mechanisms together for the earlier precision objective. Only after collecting a finished precision mechanism, clear the workstation, recover the empty andesite press with the retained wrench and craft its steel replacement. Install it at the same X-axis position in the forming layout: press plus downward USE deployer use 6 SU at 1 RPM. Eight later steel-mechanism attempts still require eight successful rolls; failures need additional parts and oil.

After the eight-precision objective and the steel-press craft, turn the remaining 24 reserved steel ingots and 24 hardened planks into 24 steel casings. Together with eight heavy plates, 24 nickel plates, 24 lead plates and the separate 6000 mB oil reserve, these supply eight complete attempts: 72 deployments, 24 fillings and 24 tier-1 pressings. Count oil across the tank, pipes and spout; the same 6000 mB redistributes through the existing circuit and is spent by twenty-four 250 mB fillings. If all eight rolls succeed, hold the eight finished mechanisms together for this non-consuming objective before later builds. One failed roll leaves only seven after these eight attempts. A returned heavy plate can start another attempt; a returned steel ingot first needs the native three-press heavy-plate sequence. Neither refunds deployed parts or oil. A ninth attempt still needs three more casings, three nickel plates, three lead plates and 750 mB oil, which require additional supplies. Preserve the sixteen separate TFMG objective ingots and the other workshop reserves.
55B8AEEB7ACA1E4E: Keep the MI steel machine casing and all sixteen canonical TFC steel ingots available. The nonconsuming four-ingot freight task may count the same held ingots.

The selected continuation adds 53 TFC steel ingots after the 45 already allocated: reserve 16 for this objective and 37 for the press and eight successful steel-mechanism attempts. Reserve two of the five spare steel shafts for press cogs; leave three free. Mechanism failures spend more components and oil, so this allocation never guarantees eight finished mechanisms.

Before continuing, stop furnace input, cast the steel output and disable the slag source port. Place one fresh empty ordinary Create tank directly below the existing slag tank. Let the two-block tank form, confirm the original 6480 mB slag is retained and capacity is 16000 mB, refresh the existing pipe connection, then resume extraction. Keep its typed network separate from steel. After 98 total batches, retain 14112 mB slag.

First close the hot-blast stove input and use the existing spout/depot to harden 25 plank blocks with 6250 mB creosote from 25 new oak logs. Hold the hardened planks, close the spout input and reopen the stove. The selected further fuel bill is 2306 oak logs plus the old 160 mB creosote. Load 63 coke dust before steel batch 46 and 57 after batch 71. New input stock also includes 212 normal hematite, 53 flux, 107 oak lumber and two copper ingots for the added tank. Boiler heat/fuel, earlier construction, mining/forestry wear, nickel, lead, oil and other mechanism hardware remain additional.

A 100-unit wrought bloom needs one 80-unit hematite briquet and one separate 20-unit pellet: 20 clean powders in total. The five-ingot terminal extension therefore needs 20 normal hematite, 100 powders and 25 pellets, arranged as five briquets plus five pellets. Its circuit-packet hammer and handstone retain 37 and 129 uses. The later 53-ingot batch needs 212 normal hematite, 1060 powders and 265 pellets, arranged as 53 briquets plus 53 pellets. Supply four fresh hammers and four fresh handstones, four new loose granite, twelve raw granite and two new oak twigs alongside the six retained handles. The hammers spend 59/59/59/35 uses and retain 1/1/1/25. The old handstone spends 83 uses and retains 46; the four new ones spend 249/249/249/230 and retain 1/1/1/20. These corrected inputs preserve the 98-ingot production schedule.

After the mechanism milestone, fund this additional casing with five NEW steel ingots: press four into plates and apply the fifth to one newly hardened plank, then recover the placed TFMG casing with your bronze pickaxe. Add two of the seven retained precision mechanisms and two fresh TFC nickel ingots. A four-ingot nickel batch leaves two spare. Keep the sixteen objective steel ingots and all eight steel mechanisms. This later batch does not supply the earlier first-bucket workshop inputs.

The additional bill is 20 normal hematite, 16 normal garnierite, five flux, eleven bituminous coal, 219 coking oak logs and four oak lumber. Make one fresh hammer and handstone from two loose granite, three raw granite and two twigs; 36 hammer uses and 180 quern uses leave 24 and 70. Fire four new ingot molds from ten clay with eight kiln logs and eight straw, and cool pottery before pickup. Reuse the insulated forge and manual bellows; nineteen new charcoal fuel a single cold-handled nickel group. Cool full molds in the unheated outputs before extraction. The five steel jobs spend 2000 of the retained 2800 mB macerator steam; slag reaches 14832 mB in the existing 16000 mB tank. Heat, ignition, earlier workshop supplies and mining/forestry wear remain additional.
0282549C54557CBB: Complete a batch of eight precision mechanisms.
Buffer every deployer input and return incomplete mechanisms to the sequence instead of discarding them.

After Automated Manipulation research, an andesite mechanical saw cuts one cold TFC wrought-iron ingot into nine ordinary iron nuggets. Use an upward-facing saw as the sole load on its own 8 RPM, 8 SU water-wheel drive, and collect each output before feeding another ingot. For the tube, millstone feed and one precision attempt, cut five new wrought ingots into 45 nuggets. Craft 36 into four ordinary iron ingots and press three of those into sheets. Two sheets plus the remaining ingot make four chutes: keep one for the millstone and three spare. The third sheet supplies the electron tube; reserve five nuggets for the attempt and leave four spare. This starts with earned TFC wrought metallurgy and avoids the precision-controlled macerator. The later steam-dust route remains available.

Sandpaper now uses one paper and one sand from the Minecraft sand tag, including TFC sand. Make rose quartz with one quartz and eight redstone, then hold it in the other hand while using fresh sandpaper until polishing finishes. The existing quartzite-milling recipe has a 5% quartz chance per run; keep milling until quartz is actually collected. Its millstone needs a separate 8 SU source from the fully loaded saw. The precision sequence still requires its gold sheet and all other supplies: five small cogs, five large cogs and five iron nuggets over 15 deployments. Its nominal precision share is four in five; a failed completed attempt spends all those inputs. Collect eight actual finished mechanisms for this objective; eight attempts do not guarantee eight results.

The first gold sheet can use a separate TFC charcoal forge before the rail workshop. Build the earlier stone furnace from eight raw rocks. Smelt 24 new TFC oak logs with 17 new TFC oak planks, made from 68 lumber, to collect 24 charcoal. Use eight charcoal for the forge pile and ten for heating; keep six spare. Add five new raw-granite insulation blocks at the sides and below. For the rain roof, chisel five loose granite into five stone bricks. In the earlier barrel, make limewater from one flux and 500 mB water; seal one TFC sand with 100 mB limewater for longer than 7200 calendar ticks to obtain 16 mortar. Four mortar and the five stone bricks craft four granite-brick blocks. Place a temporary brick scaffold at Y1 above the full charcoal pile, place the roof at Y2, then recover the scaffold before ignition. Keep Y1 above the forge empty and the adjacent west sky column open; three brick blocks remain spare. These are new inputs, separate from later rail and oil reserves.

Mine 16 additional normal native-gold ores and use the guaranteed hammer, sluice, quern and second sluice route to collect 80 clean gold powders. Fund a new stone hammer with one loose granite and a twig, and a new handstone with three raw granite and a second twig; this gold batch spends 16 hammer uses and 80 handstone uses. Knap four fresh ingot molds from ten clay and fire them in one kiln load with eight additional logs and eight straw. Let the molds cool before handling. With the covered forge and its ten counted fuel charcoal, melt five one-item powders at a time into the four output molds. Stop fueling after the counted batch and leave all molds in the forge until cold before pickup. No hot vessel transfer or bellows is needed for this gold route. All four molds may break after delivering four ingots. Press one ingot for the original attempt and reserve the other three for the wrench below. Additional attempts need new gold, cogs and nuggets.

The wrench can use the three cold gold ingots left by the new primitive batch: press them into three sheets. After Automated Manipulation research, the wrench recipe accepts a tier-0 Greate small cog. Make one extra cog with one of the two new shaft spares, one additional andesite alloy and one plank from four additional lumber, then add one wooden rod for the wrench. One shaft spare remains and no gold ingot remains. The combined first-attempt and wrench bill is 60 alloy and 228 lumber. Keep the five small cogs, five large cogs and five nuggets reserved for the attempt; do not take this wrench from later workshop reserves.

Build the forming drive with every shaft and cog on axis X. Relative positions: water wheel (-8,-3,-3); small cogs (-6,-3,-3), (-4,-2,-2), (-2,-1,-1); large cogs (-6,-2,-2), (-4,-1,-1), (-2,0,0); five shafts (-7,-3,-3), (-5,-2,-2), (-3,-1,-1), (-1,0,0), (1,0,0). Put the earlier andesite press at (0,0,0) and the downward USE deployer at (2,0,0), with its horizontal shaft axis X. Place depots two blocks below the press and deployer. The press and deployer work before the oil spout exists; leave (4,0,0)/(4,-2,0) empty. When oil handling is ready, translate this layout to the spout/depot while preserving its tank and pipes. Three small-to-large reductions give 1 RPM: press plus deployer use 5 SU of the 8 SU drive. Later replace the empty andesite press with the steel press at the same position for 6 SU total. Normal wrench clicks on the body rotate the deployer or its shaft axis; the protruding hand can toggle mode, so verify USE after adjustments. Sneaking can dismantle blocks. Keep work cells clear and preserve the same workpiece’s sequence marker when moving it between depots.

For the minimum eight-success branch, keep the first funded attempt and add supplies for seven more: 131 andesite alloy, 13 foundry lids, 600 lumber and four cold TFC wrought-iron ingots. Make 13 batches of eight shafts, 105 small cogs and 35 large cogs. Each large cog consumes two small ones: 70 small cogs become the 35 large ones, leaving 35 small cogs for deployment. Cut the four wrought ingots into 36 nuggets; with the four old spares, 35 are spent and five remain. The seven earlier spare shafts plus 104 new ones leave six after crafting. Use 560 lumber for cog planks and reserve 40 lumber for ten furnace-fuel planks. Keep the installed drive cogs and prepared steel-press parts separate.

Reuse the cleared cold primitive forge and its roof. Process 32 new normal gold ores into 160 clean powders; the retained gold hammer and handstone spend 32 and 160 uses, leaving 12 and 10. Make eight fresh molds from 20 clay and fire two four-mold kiln loads with 16 logs and 16 straw; all molds may break. After the old furnace fuel expires, smelt 14 more logs with the ten new planks. Combine the 14 charcoal with the six saved spares. Repeat the earlier four-gold cold-forge schedule twice, each with ten charcoal, a successful strong ignition and the full cooling wait. Eight new cold ingots fund seven sheets and leave one ingot. Hold eight finished precision mechanisms together for this non-consuming objective before spending one on the steel press; seven then remain. A branch allowing one failed attempt instead needs 150 alloy, 15 lids and 680 lumber for eight further attempts; its gold, pottery, fuel and four-wrought bill is unchanged. These alternate bills never guarantee success: replenish missing inputs after further failures.
0595297A22D475B5: Assemble and place the bronze boiler from the live pack recipe.
Connect buffered water before fuel, give steam a destination, and stay nearby long enough to inspect the running installation.

Make clear glass through TFC glassworking: potash, lime heated from flux, and white sand make four silica glass batches. Use one batch for a basin pour and one for a table pour; keep the other two. Fire ceramic blowpipes at 1399 C and provide two pipes so breakage after either successful pour cannot stop the second. Keep the loaded pipe in hand and above 480 C, below its 1500 C melting recipe.

The basin needs five brass blocks around an empty cell. Pour once, let the glass cool, then break it normally to collect a glass block. Use a separate isolated brass block as the pouring table, with air above; table-pour, flatten promptly with a paddle, let it cool and break it for a glass pane. TFC disables the vanilla pane craft. Reserve the block for the bronze tank and the pane for the MI fluid-pipe batch; the remaining boiler materials and fuel still need supplying.
0C4F7FBDB9DA914D: Use industrial steel to turn local machinery and bulk hauling into reliable services.
Cast sixteen canonical TFC steel ingots through the TFMG industrial-blasting and casting route.
Feed crushed raw iron or iron dust with TFMG coal coke, collect molten steel separately from slag and furnace gas, then cast 144 mB per ingot.

Upgrade the forming line to a Steel Greate Press. It finishes steel mechanisms, steam locomotives and the supported engine assemblies; the same press later finishes the first rocket. It needs precision mechanisms to build, so commission it before its steel-mechanism output.

Connect fuel, loading, unloading and cargo buffers into a serviced freight route. As demand grows, use the existing steel- and precision-mechanism assembler batches; retain the first assembly line for repairs and restart stock.
1A57E0F180BD83FE: Hold a steel upgrade and one canonical TFC steel ingot after commissioning the main line.
The decorative reward closes this branch; LV circuits, wire, batteries, and generators still require their own work.
13600CBD07081E1A: Build another steel macerator and hold sixteen canonical TFC steel ingots for its supply chain.
Confirm boiler and turbine capacity before connecting both ore lines at once.
65C742774D5BE2B7: Stock thirty-two canonical TFC steel ingots and thirty-two MI steel plates.
Maintain the coke, iron, hot-air, casting, and forming inputs that can replace this reserve.
2EA08DCC6E926259: Store four steel large plates with sixteen canonical TFC steel ingots.
Use them only after the boiler is cool, empty, and isolated from the shared steam trunk.
077A050000000001: Land on Venus by rocket and find the ruined containment station in newly generated terrain.
Its rings, panels, power cells, and liquid-energy hardware are inert by design, leaving only architectural and symbolic evidence.
Recover a Red Sandstone Symbol and measure how the installation survived heat, pressure, and corrosive chemistry.
The station contains one Red Sandstone Symbol. Recover it with a bronze pickaxe or better, then survey another station for the second symbol. Mine Venus Stone directly; Silk Touch is not required.
077A060000000001: Craft five Venusian Field Data packs from two recovered Red Sandstone Symbols, one Venus Stone, four paper, one Memory Crystal and one Electronic Circuit.
Complete FRN-04C — Dimensional Field Theory. Craft the unlocked Energy Crystal as a controlled laboratory reconstruction.
One field component cannot operate a gate; it only proves the containment model.
077A070000000001: Reach Mercury by rocket and locate the ancient calibration relay in newly generated terrain.
Recover its Red Sandstone Cartouche and compare the glyph arrangement against stellar coordinates, chevron order, and a point of origin.
The Solar-System sites now form one navigational theory, but the machine remains beyond present manufacturing.
